issues.legal_issue: Acquisition of property declared to be evacuee property under a law protected by the constitutional exception is not invalidated by the absence of an agreement providing for compensation.
material_facts: The property had been declared evacuee property and was acquired by a published government notification for the rehabilitation of displaced persons.
The applicable law provided for compensation according to principles and in a manner agreed between the governments of the two countries, but no such agreement had been reached.
The constitutional exception covered laws concerning evacuee property made in pursuance of an agreement or otherwise.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition was not open to challenge under Article 31(2), and compensation could not be claimed under the applicable law in the absence of the contemplated agreement.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31(5)(b)(iii) excluded from the operation of Article 31(2) laws concerning property declared by law to be evacuee property, whether made pursuant to an agreement with another country or otherwise. Sections 12 and 13 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1951 provided for acquisition and for compensation in accordance with principles and a manner agreed between the governments; without that agreement, compensation was not payable under Section 13. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: challenge_to_acquisition_of_evacuee_property and acquisition_law_covers_evacuee_property and constitutional_exception_covers_such_laws and not compensation_agreement_exists

predicates.challenge_to_acquisition_of_evacuee_prop: A person challenges the acquisition of property that had been declared evacuee property.
predicates.acquisition_law_covers_evacuee_property: The law under which the property was acquired applies to property declared evacuee property.
predicates.constitutional_exception_covers_such_law: The constitutional exception protects laws concerning evacuee property whether made pursuant to an agreement with another country or otherwise.
predicates.compensation_agreement_exists: The governments whose agreement is required have agreed on the principles and manner for paying compensation.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns acquisition of evacuee property under a law covered by the constitutional exception, and the required compensation agreement does not exist, the challenge under the specified constitutional protection fails and compensation is not claimable under that law.

issues.legal_issue: Statutory acquisition of evacuee property vests the property in the government upon publication of the acquisition notification, without awaiting determination or payment of compensation.
material_facts: A notification acquiring property declared evacuee property was published.
The applicable law provided that publication extinguished the evacuee's right, title and interest and vested the property absolutely in the government.
The principles for compensation had not been agreed, and compensation had not been determined or paid.
issues.conclusion: The property vested absolutely in the government upon publication of the notification, regardless of whether compensation had been determined or paid.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(2) of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1951 provided that publication of a notification under Section 12(1) extinguished the evacuee's right, title and interest and vested the property absolutely in the government, free from encumbrances. The provision did not make vesting conditional on fixing or paying compensation. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.challenge_to_statutory_acquisition_of_ev: A person challenges the vesting of property acquired under a law concerning property declared evacuee property.
predicates.acquisition_notification_published: The government published a notification acquiring the property.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns statutory acquisition of evacuee property and the acquisition notification has been published, the property vests in the government on publication without waiting for compensation.
